svg.aria-label: Geaix VS Code extension attack chain
svg.title: Geaix VS Code / Antigravity Extension — Attack Chain
svg.desc: Flowchart: trojanised VSIX extension drops a signed javaw.exe plus a malicious jli.dll, side-loads to reflectively map an in-memory infostealer that exfiltrates to dtapi.cc, x1zsp.cc and cfmlapi.cc.

g.text: Geaix VS Code / Antigravity Extension — Attack Chain
Trojanised geaix.geaix-1.0.24 → DLL side-loading → in-memory infostealer, clipper & runner
Victim downloads a VS Code extension from geaix.com
looks like a real AI coding agent (rebadged Kilo Code fork)
Installed into VS Code / Google Antigravity
activationEvents: onLanguage, onStartupFinished → runs on every editor start
④ Extract with yauzl into %TEMP%\<decoy>-<hex>\ (12-prefix pool)
⑤ Cache path + SHA-256 in globalState so later launches skip the fetch
Three files land in the decoy %TEMP% folder
plus 15 min WebSocket telemetry to wss://geaix.com/api/ws
Windows loader sees jli.dll next to javaw.exe and resolves it from that directory.
Execution enters the attacker's JLI_Launch export, running inside a signed, trusted process.
In-memory unpack and reflective PE map
① Decode a 594,786-character .rdata text blob (custom 64-char alphabet, 6-bit packing)
② Decompress with a custom LZ77 → 606,720 bytes of sections for build.dll (never written to disk)
③ VirtualAlloc one 0x9B400-byte RWX region, restore the zeroed MZ/PE header, map 8 sections
④ Resolve 94 imports, apply 855 relocations, fake an LDR entry, call DllMain once
Stage 3 — build.dll runs inside the signed javaw.exe
